title: Design a house, then let your villagers build it — StoneEra Demo 0.9.14.2
author: Arrock12
selftext:
I’m the solo developer of StoneEra, a medieval voxel colony sim. Here’s a short look at designing a house in its Building Editor.  
You can save your designs as reusable plans, place them in your settlement, and let villagers handle construction. Builders now put up temporary scaffolding to reach higher floors, then dismantle it and return the planks to storage.  
The **0.9.14.2 — Error Fix & Building Tools** demo update also brings:  
A cleaner Building Editor with searchable item cards, clearer previews, and local plan import/export.  
Three times the durability for new and starting tools.  
**Keep in Stock** production targets that automatically replenish crafted supplies.  
Multiple villagers researching a technology together.  
Better storage sorting and fixes for villager movement, sleep, and blocked bed exits.  
The editor, building plans, and scaffolding are still very early alpha, so expect bugs and rough edges.  
There’s a [free demo on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5057770/StoneEra/) with no session timer and 12 early technologies through ore smelting.  
What would you want from a building planner in a colony sim?

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Tried the demo. 

 \- While the building editor is a very excellent concept in a game like this, having it completely decoupled from the gameplay, and also forcing the player to engage with it, is terrible implementation. I went into a new colony expecting there to be some prefabs only to be told I need to already have buildings made in the editor before play can even start. No. No, no, no. 

The editor should be accessible during play, probably directly from the building menu itself, and should not be mandatory. You need to include prefabs that the player can just plop down. It's fine if the prefabs are simple and inefficient; that will make it fun for people who want to optimize or beautify their experience, because there's a baseline to compare against. For everyone else who just wants to play, ploppable prefabs mean they can just... play. 

 \- Voxels are a good aesthetic choice. Do you mind if I ask what the workflow was, and how much of a hassle it was to get voxels to work? 

 \- Some of the orders UI choices are awkward. Cutting, for example, just draws a line and doesn't seem to select multiple trees except when it wants to. It should be a box selection. 

 \- Pacing is too slow, especially for a demo meant to show off early mechanics. It takes ages to plant a field, as an example. Colonists should be uber-colonists at this stage just so progress can be made and the game explored - when things are more refined, you can start winding down the colonists into proper niches and set more substantive times against colonists who don't have the right skill to match a given task. 

 \- There's a lot going on with the UI right now. I know it is a colony management game and so a busy UI feels almost mandatory / inevitable, but personally I'd try to see what you can peel back on or otherwise improve in that area. Making a colony management sim make accessible, if you could pull it off, would be a tremendous achievement - and something like a building editor with the potential for prefabs already puts you a step in the right direction. 

  
It looks promising, but I don't think this is demo-ready at all, IMHO (though it's understanable if you have no playtest audience other than what you can find in the wild).

replies.author: Arrock12
replies.body:
Thanks for taking the time to try the demo and share such detailed feedback!  
The Building Editor is still a very new feature, and I’m actively working on improving it. I’m also planning to let players turn buildings they’ve constructed during gameplay into reusable templates.  
There are actually Line and Box selection tools in the tree-cutting menu, so you can select multiple trees at once.  
Yes, I completely agree about the pacing, and I’m already working on improving it.  
The UI is also something I’m constantly refining and improving with each update.  
Thanks again for the constructive feedback. It really helps me see where the experience needs more work!
